facts: Neogen delivered Q1 revenue of approximately $209 million, up 0.3% year-over-year on a core basis, which was in line with expectations.
The company executed a global headcount reduction of approximately 10% of existing and planned positions, expected to reduce operating expenses by approximately $20 million on an annualized basis.
Adjusted EBITDA was $35.5 million in Q1, representing a margin of 17%, down from prior year due to lower volume, gross margin headwinds, and higher operating expenses.
Petrifilm, which has had a core revenue CAGR in the mid-single-digit range over recent years, experienced a mid-single-digit decline in Q1 attributed to distributor inventory rebalancing.
Q1 free cash flow was an outflow of $13 million, representing an improvement of $43 million compared to the prior year Q1.

The company completed the divestiture of its cleaners and disinfectants business for approximately $115 million in net proceeds, using $100 million to pay down debt with annualized interest savings of roughly $6 million.
Neogen ended Q1 with gross debt of $800 million (68% at fixed rate) and a total cash position of $139 million.

Food Safety segment revenues were $152 million, down 4.6% compared to prior year including a core decline of 1.7%, while Animal Safety segment revenues were $57 million with core revenue growth of 5.8%.
The company expects to realize approximately $12 million benefit from cost reduction actions this fiscal year, with more than half already contemplated in initial guidance.
Adjusted earnings per share were $0.04 in Q1 compared to $0.07 in the prior year quarter, primarily due to lower adjusted EBITDA which more than offset lower interest expense.

Q1 2026 revenue was $1.35 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $28 million, down from $31.2 million in Q1 2025, while the company reiterated full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $275 million to $325 million.
SG&A was reduced by more than $29 million (7.5%) year-over-year, including $19 million in compensation reductions, with SG&A as a percentage of gross profit improving by 135 basis points.

The company executed an additional $10 million of annualized cost rationalization in the quarter, bringing year-to-date annualized cost savings to nearly $35 million, with further IT-related AI-driven savings expected.

New vehicle gross margin declined 148 basis points to 12.2% and used vehicle gross margin declined 91 basis points to 17.7%, with margin pressure expected to continue through Q2 before improving in the back half of 2026.

Same-store used sales fell 2.6% in Q1 due to January/February weather disruptions that shut down 60+ stores, but April same-store used unit sales are trending up high single digits year-over-year with new flat to slightly down.

Total same-store RV unit inventory is down over 10% year-over-year, year-to-date purchases are down over 20%, and model year 2025 inventory has been reduced over 50% in units to roughly 8% of total new inventory.
Net debt leverage ratio improved to 5.6x from 8.1x a year ago, the company ended Q1 with $200 million of cash, and paid down $56 million of debt in the quarter.
Management narrowed 2026 industry outlook to the lower end of 325,000-350,000 new RV units and the midpoint of 715,000-750,000 used units, while new vehicle ASPs rose approximately 4% year-over-year.
Net CapEx is targeted to be south of $100 million for 2026 (excluding sale-leasebacks), with maintenance CapEx estimated closer to $75 million going forward.
Model year 2027 motorized units are showing only a 1-2% price increase versus a 5-7% increase for model year 2026, while towables could see 1-3% increases, supporting affordability.
Q3 2025 net sales decreased 5% year-over-year to $1.11 billion, with residential net sales declining 13% while global C&I product sales increased 9%.
The company's backlog for large megawatt generators for data centers doubled to over $300 million over the last 90 days, with the majority expected to ship in 2026.
Q3 2025 experienced the lowest third quarter of total outage hours since 2015, approximately 75% to 80% below normal baseline levels.
Adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 17.3% in Q3 2025 from 19.8% in the prior year quarter, primarily due to unfavorable sales mix and operating expense deleverage.
Full year 2025 net sales guidance was revised to approximately flat compared to prior year, down from the previous guidance of 2% to 5% growth.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was reduced to approximately 17%, down from the prior guidance range of 18% to 19%.
The residential dealer network expanded to nearly 9,400 dealers, an increase of approximately 100 from the prior quarter and nearly 300 over the prior year.
Ecobee's installed base grew to approximately 4.75 million connected homes and is expected to deliver positive EBITDA contribution for the full year 2025.
The company expects C&I production capacity for large megawatt generators could reach $500 million or more in 2026, with potential to double C&I product sales over the next 3 to 5 years.
Free cash flow conversion guidance was reduced to approximately 80% for full year 2025 from the previous 90% to 100% range, still expected to generate approximately $300 million in free cash flow.
Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue was $147 million, essentially flat year-over-year, while adjusted EBITDA increased to $13.4 million.
Free cash flow was $23 million in Q2, and the company reduced total debt by $22.7 million, ending with a net leverage ratio of 0.4x.
Lighting segment delivered 15% sales growth year-over-year, marking the third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
Lighting adjusted operating income increased 29% with adjusted gross margin improving 190 basis points versus the prior year.
Lighting orders for Q2 were up approximately 10% year-over-year, resulting in a book-to-bill ratio above 1 and an improved backlog.
Display Solutions adjusted gross margin improved 30 basis points despite lower production volume due to improved productivity from more stable scheduling.
Q2 grocery orders increased double digits year-over-year, generating a book-to-bill ratio of 1.2 versus under 1 last year.
Premium food services opportunities in casual dining range from $250,000 to $1 million per location versus QSR programs at $20,000 to $40,000 per location.
The company has cash and availability of approximately $100 million following its amended financing facility.
LSI is on pace for its fourth consecutive year of free cash flow exceeding $30 million.
Full year 2025 total revenue was $1.5 billion, with core commission and fee organic revenue growth of 8% and total organic revenue growth of 7%.
The company's 2026 guidance includes total revenue between $2.01 billion and $2.05 billion, adjusted EBITDA between $460 million and $480 million, and adjusted diluted EPS between $2.00 and $2.10.
The Board authorized a $250 million share repurchase plan, and CEO Trevor Baldwin stated that at 8x EBITDA there is no better use of capital than buying back the company's own shares.

The three partnerships closed on January 1 (CAC Group, OBE, and Capstone) delivered approximately $350 million of 2025 pro forma revenue and are expected to generate roughly $400 million of revenue and approximately $110 million of adjusted EBITDA post synergies in 2026.

CAC integration is ahead of schedule, with $25 million of the $43 million in targeted cost synergies already actioned within two months, and the CAC team has $32 million in closed new business in 2026 versus $20 million in the prior year period.

A 10-year exclusive agreement was signed with Fairway Independent Mortgage Corporation, the sixth largest independent mortgage lender in the U.S. with over 67,000 loans originated in 2024, with go-live expected in Q2.
Fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 basis points to 20.1%, and the Main Street Insurance segment saw adjusted EBITDA margin expand 460 basis points to 31.8% despite top-line headwinds.

Net leverage stood at 4.1x at quarter end, with the company increasing its term loan facility by $600 million in December to fund the CAC, OBE, and Capstone closings at a pricing of SOFR plus 250 basis points.

The company expects organic revenue growth to ramp throughout 2026 to reach double digits by the fourth quarter as it laps the QBE commission headwind in MIS and the procedural accounting change in IAS.

Investment in frontline revenue-generating talent increased by 44% in 2025, raising net unvalidated producer pay from 1.6% to 2.3% of commission and fee revenue, while IAS sales velocity was 19% versus an industry median of approximately 11%.

Joby ended Q1 2026 with approximately $2.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, including $1.3 billion in net proceeds raised during the quarter from equity and convertible offerings and Delta Airlines warrant exercises.

Q1 revenue was $24 million, down $7 million sequentially due to the absence of one-time Q4 Japan flight demonstration revenue, with full year 2026 revenue guidance maintained at $105 million to $115 million.
Q1 GAAP net loss was $110 million, a $12 million improvement vs. Q4's $122 million loss, while adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $179 million from $154 million in Q4.

Q1 cash use excluding capital raises was approximately $195 million (or $163 million excluding the $32 million net Ohio facility purchase), tracking within the first half 2026 guidance of $340 million to $370 million.

Joby was selected for the White House-backed eIPP program as part of 5 applications covering 11 states including Texas, New York and Florida, with OTA agreements expected to begin being signed in Q3 2026 and operations starting in the back half of 2026.

The company is producing parts for its ninth conforming aircraft, has 5 aircraft designated for TIA flight testing, and its composites team is producing 2.5x the volume of parts it was a year ago, having added a third shift.
Joby successfully completed its SR3 audit with the FAA during the quarter, confirming test results meet expectations for the fifth and final stage of type certification.

Joby completed full transition flights with its turbine-electric VTOL aircraft, including a 148-mile flight at max takeoff weight of 2,400 kilograms, and demonstrated it to the U.S. Army with partner L3Harris.
Joby demonstrated the first ever eVTOL flight between an international airport (JFK) and a downtown heliport, operating in Class B airspace and connecting JFK to multiple Manhattan heliports.

Management has two paths to potential passenger flights later in 2026: Dubai (where the first purpose-built commercial vertiport next to Dubai International Airport was completed) and U.S. eIPP markets including New York, Florida and Texas.
Marriott's global portfolio stood at nearly 1.78 million rooms across more than 9,800 properties in 145 countries and territories at the end of December 2025.
The development pipeline grew to a record 610,000 rooms, up 6% year-over-year, with nearly 265,000 rooms under construction, up 15% year-over-year.
For full year 2026, net rooms growth is expected to accelerate to 4.5% to 5%, all organic, with full year global RevPAR growth expected between 1.5% and 2.5%.
Full year 2025 gross fee revenues rose 5% to $5.4 billion, adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to $5.38 billion, and adjusted EPS rose 7% to $10.02.

Co-branded credit card fees are expected to increase approximately 35% year-over-year in 2026, driven by continued high single-digit spending growth and an increase in Marriott's royalty rate on credit card payments.
Marriott Bonvoy membership reached 271 million members worldwide at year-end, with 43 million new members joining in 2025 alone, and Bonvoy penetration increasing from 58% in 2019 to 68%.
Full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA is expected to increase 8% to 10% to roughly $5.8 billion to $5.9 billion, with adjusted diluted EPS growth expected between 13% and 15%.
Government RevPAR was down over 30% during the 43-day U.S. government shutdown and has since moderated to down around 15%.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup is expected to contribute around 30 to 35 basis points of global RevPAR growth for the full year, and group pace for 2026 is up 6% year-over-year.
Marriott returned over $4 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in 2025 and expects over $4.3 billion in capital returns in 2026.
Total revenue for fiscal Q1 2026 was $44.2 million, up 19% year-over-year.
Fraud and Identity revenue grew 30% year-over-year to $25.5 million, while SaaS revenue grew 21% year-over-year and now represents 43% of last 12 months revenue.
Adjusted EBITDA was $13.3 million, up 69% year-over-year, representing a 30% margin and a roughly 900 basis point improvement versus the prior year.
Check Fraud Defender annualized contract value reached approximately $17 million, up 44% year-over-year, with consortium data sets now covering in excess of 50% of U.S. checking accounts.
The company retired its $155 million convertible senior notes in full, drew $50 million on its term loan, and announced a new $50 million share repurchase authorization.
Check Verification revenue was $18.8 million in Q1, up 6% year-over-year, with LTM revenue stable at approximately $91 million and annual transaction volumes of approximately 1.2 billion.
Fiscal 2026 revenue guidance was raised by $2 million to a range of $187 million to $197 million, with Fraud and Identity expected at $102 million to $107 million.
Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance for fiscal 2026 was increased to 29%-32%, up from 27%-30%, driven primarily by higher capitalized software development.
Free cash flow was $6.6 million for the quarter and $60.5 million on a last 12-month basis, representing 102% conversion of LTM adjusted EBITDA compared to 83% last year.
Non-GAAP net income resulted in adjusted EPS of $0.26 per diluted share, representing approximately 80% growth year-over-year.
Alight generated full year 2025 revenue of approximately $2.3 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $561 million (24.8% margin), and free cash flow of $250 million.
Full year 2025 recurring revenue of approximately $2.1 billion was down 2.2% year-over-year, while project revenue of $154 million was down 22% year-over-year.
Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $178 million versus $217 million in Q4 2024, adversely impacted by approximately $45 million in increased compensation expense that management views as recurring.
The company recognized a noncash goodwill impairment charge of $803 million in Q4 2025, leaving only $83 million of remaining goodwill on the balance sheet.
Management expects Q1 2026 revenue to decline in the high single-digit percentage range year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA margins declining 500 to 750 basis points compared to Q1 2025.
Revenue under contract entering 2026 is approximately 5% lower than the prior year, driven by a renewal rate that was significantly below the company's mid- to high-90s percentage target.
The 2026 renewal cohort is approximately 30% to 40% lighter than the 2025 cohort.
The company is eliminating its quarterly dividend in favor of debt reduction and opportunistic share repurchases, with $216 million remaining under its existing buyback authorization.

A TRA payment of approximately $156 million is expected in 2026 related to the 2024 tax year and the Strada divestiture gain, but no significant TRA payments are expected in 2027 or 2028 due to tax reform.

The company plans to deploy more than $100 million of capital investment in 2026 to strengthen foundations including sales and account management hiring, AI-enabled product innovation, and user experience improvements.
Third quarter 2025 revenue was $694 million and year-to-date revenue stands at $2.2 billion, representing a 58% and 64% increase respectively, driven by the Marcum acquisition.

Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA margin increased approximately 325 basis points versus last year, with lower incentive compensation expense representing approximately 250 of the 325 basis point improvement.
Third quarter adjusted diluted earnings per share was $1.01, bringing year-to-date adjusted EPS to $4.27 per share.
The company updated its synergy goal from the Marcum acquisition to a total of $50 million or more, up from the previous $25 million target, with $35 million expected to be realized in 2025.
Integration cost estimates for 2025 increased by $14 million to $89 million, primarily driven by additional severance costs related to streamlining combined staffing levels.
The company ended the quarter with net debt at approximately $1.6 billion and approximately $300 million of available liquidity under its revolver.
In the third quarter, CBIZ repurchased approximately 800,000 shares at a value of approximately $56 million, bringing year-to-date share repurchases to $128 million or 1.8 million shares.
The company is maintaining its revenue guidance for the year at $2.8 billion to $2.95 billion, with line of sight to the low end of the range.
Financial Services segment third quarter revenue was $579 million, up approximately 80%, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.7%.
The company achieved strong mid-single-digit rate increases in the quarter and year-to-date, exceeding overall inflation according to management.
Restaurant contribution margin improved 160 basis points year-over-year to 18.3% in Q3 2025, compared to 16.7% in the year ago period.
Digital business including kiosks grew to 27% of system sales in Q3 2025 compared to 20% in the same period last year.
System-wide comparable store sales for Q4 to date through October 22, 2025 increased 2.2%, consisting of a 1.5% increase in company-operated restaurants and a 2.5% increase in franchise restaurants.
GAAP net income increased to $7.4 million or $0.25 per diluted share in Q3 2025 compared to $6.2 million or $0.21 per diluted share in the prior year period.
Labor and related expenses decreased approximately 200 basis points year-over-year to 30.4% of company restaurant sales due to labor deployment improvements, technology use, and menu price increases.
All new restaurants opened in 2024 and 2025 are averaging $2 million on an annualized basis.
Loyalty transactions increased 28% year-over-year with customer frequency up 15%.
The company plans to almost double its development pace in 2026 and expects to open at least 10 new restaurants system-wide in 2025.
Full year 2025 restaurant-level contribution margins are expected to be 17.5% to 17.75%, with long-term expectations to return to 18% to 20% range.
Franchise traffic growth accelerated to 2.5% in Q3, which drove positive system-wide traffic growth of 1.6% for the quarter.
Hubbell delivered Q3 adjusted diluted EPS growth of 12% year-over-year, driven by high single-digit organic growth and a lower tax rate.
Free cash flow increased 34% in Q3 to $254 million, on track to deliver 90% of net income conversion for the full year.
Full year 2025 adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $18.10-$18.30, a $0.30 increase at the midpoint primarily from a lower expected tax rate.
The DMC Power acquisition closed in October for $825 million and is expected to contribute approximately $0.20 of adjusted EPS accretion in 2026.
Grid Automation sales declined 18% in Q3 due to large project roll-offs, creating about a 4% drag on overall company growth.
The Electrical Solutions segment achieved 10% sales growth and 17% operating profit growth with approximately 140 basis points of margin expansion in Q3.
Share repurchases in the first half of 2025 totaled approximately $225 million, contributing to EPS growth.
Q4 2025 guidance implies 8% to 10% organic growth with contributions from both segments as Grid Automation headwinds fade.
T&D Infrastructure has grown at a double-digit CAGR over the last 5 years, and orders accelerated substantially in September and October.
The lower tax rate in 2025 was driven by an international acquisition restructuring and is expected to normalize in 2026.
Q3 2025 net revenue was $239.5 million, representing 29% year-over-year growth.
Full year 2025 revenue guidance was raised from $820-860 million to $845-865 million.
Cash and cash equivalents totaled $778 million as of September 30, 2025, with $106 million generated in Q3.
WAKIX achieved a record quarterly increase of approximately 500 average patients, reaching 8,100 average patients by end of Q3.
Non-GAAP adjusted net income for Q3 2025 was $63.5 million or $1.08 per diluted share, compared to $57.3 million or $0.99 per diluted share in the prior year quarter.
Total operating expenses for Q3 2025 were $114.3 million compared to $81.6 million in the same quarter of 2024, including a $15 million milestone for ZYN002 trial enrollment completion.
In the pitolisant GR dosing optimization study, 100% of patients (46 of 46) tolerated the 17.8mg therapeutic dose, and 98% tolerated the higher 35.6mg dose at week 2.
The ZYN002 Phase III RECONNECT study in Fragile X syndrome did not meet its primary endpoint of improvement in social avoidance due to higher-than-expected placebo response.
Utility patents have been filed for both pitolisant GR and pitolisant HD with potential exclusivity through 2044, with target PDUFA dates in Q1 2027 for GR and 2028 for HD programs.
The company expects to have 5 ongoing Phase III registrational programs by year-end 2025, with 2 new Phase III trials for pitolisant HD planned for Q4 in narcolepsy and idiopathic hypersomnia.
Total premiums and deposits reached $12.3 billion in Q3 2025, the highest since the IPO.
RILA product sales were nearly $800 million in Q3 and have topped $1.7 billion year-to-date.
General account net inflows were $1.4 billion, up 27% year-over-year, supporting general account growth of 6%.
Run rate operating EPS of $1.21 represents a 6% year-over-year increase, with adjusted run rate ROE of 12.9%, up 70 basis points versus prior year.
Year-to-date, the company returned more than $1.4 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends, with an 80% payout ratio reflecting the VA reinsurance transaction impact.
Holding company liquidity remains at $1.8 billion, including partial proceeds from the VA reinsurance transaction.
The investment portfolio is 95% investment grade and highly diversified among asset class, industrial sectors, and geographies.
Institutional Markets had its strongest sales quarter since the IPO, with the sixth consecutive quarter of GIC issuances exceeding $1 billion and total reserves growing by $8 billion or 19%.
The annual actuarial assumption update resulted in a charge of $98 million, though it is expected to have limited impact on go-forward run rate earnings.
CFO Elias Habayeb will leave Corebridge in April 2026, with a 6-month transition period to oversee 2025 financial statements and 2026 budget finalization.
Q3 2025 total revenue was $2 million, down 52.5% from Q3 2024 and down 45% from Q2 2025.
Q4 2025 revenue guidance range is $3.5 million to $6 million, with the wide range dependent on a single contract valued at nearly $3 million that may slip into Q1 2026.
Non-GAAP gross margin in Q3 was negative 11.9%, compared to 65.3% in Q3 2024, primarily due to unfavorable absorption of fixed costs and $300,000 of R&D costs allocated to COGS.
Non-GAAP net loss for Q3 was $3.2 million or $0.19 per diluted share, compared to a loss of $0.9 million or $0.06 per share in Q3 2024.
Total cash at quarter end was $17.3 million, inclusive of $15 million utilized from a $20 million credit facility.
The company raised approximately $2 million using its ATM program in October to prepare for potential delayed payments from the U.S. government contract.
A mid-7-figure Intel 18A contract previously expected in Q4 has been delayed into 2026 due to funding timing issues.
Management expects storefront revenue to begin in early 2026 and provide meaningful contribution (approximately 10% of total 2026 revenue).
At the high end of Q4 guidance ($6 million revenue), the company projects a non-GAAP net profit of approximately $600,000 or $0.04 per share.
The company expects Q4 non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $3 million and full-year 2025 non-GAAP OpEx of approximately $11.3 million.
Q1 2026 sales were $6 billion with core revenue up 0.5% year-over-year, including a 2.5% headwind from respiratory revenue partially offsetting 3% core growth in the rest of the business.
Adjusted diluted EPS grew 9.5% year-over-year to $2.06, and Danaher raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.35–$8.55 from the prior $8.35–$8.50.
Full-year 2026 core revenue growth guidance was maintained at 3%–6%, with a lowered respiratory revenue assumption of approximately $1.6–$1.7 billion offset by modestly better growth elsewhere.
Q2 2026 guidance calls for low single-digit core revenue growth and an adjusted operating profit margin of approximately 26.5%, down from Q1's 30.2% (which expanded 60 basis points year-over-year).

Bioprocessing core revenue grew high single digits, with consumables up high single digits and equipment orders growing more than 30% year-over-year—the first quarter of equipment order growth in nearly two years.

Cepheid's respiratory revenue declined approximately 25% year-over-year due to a light Q1 season, while its core non-respiratory menu grew mid-teens, led by ~20% growth in sexual health and hospital-acquired infection assays.
Diagnostics core revenue declined 4%, with China facing an expected high single-digit decline from volume-based procurement, while clinical diagnostics outside China grew mid-single digits.
Life Sciences core revenue rose 0.5%, with China Life Sciences and Biotechnology accelerating and Abcam and Aldevron returning to growth amid improved biotech funding.

The pending Masimo acquisition is expected to be EPS accretive in the first full year and deliver high single-digit ROIC by year five, with ~$125 million of cost synergies and ~$50 million of revenue synergies; post-close net leverage is expected at ~2.5x EBITDA.
Danaher generated $1.1 billion of free cash flow in Q1 (105% conversion) and expects more than $5 billion of free cash flow in 2026, supporting continued M&A capacity across all three segments.
Q3 reported revenue was $1.62 billion, down 5% year-over-year on an organic basis, reflecting weaker-than-expected top line performance primarily in lab.
The company took a $785 million noncash goodwill impairment charge associated with its lab distribution business due to continued share price weakness and margin headwinds.
The Board authorized a $500 million share repurchase program with immediate effect.
Free cash flow was $172 million in Q3 with adjusted conversion at 124% of adjusted net income.
The company won approximately $100 million in business at two top 15 global pharma customers, which will start phasing in during 2026.
Full year organic revenue growth guidance was reduced to negative 3.5% to negative 2.5%, with adjusted EPS guidance lowered to $0.88-$0.92.
Adjusted gross margin declined 100 basis points year-over-year to 32.4%, driven mainly by price actions in lab to protect market share.
Bioprocessing book-to-bill is 1.0 year-to-date and in Q3, with process chemicals orders up high single digits while billings are only up low single digits.
Q4 bioprocessing is expected to be down high single digits to low double digits year-over-year, with process chemicals expected down double digits despite solid order performance.
Adjusted net leverage ended Q3 at 3.1x adjusted EBITDA, with no debt maturities before 2028 following a refinancing that upsized the revolving credit facility to $1.4 billion extended to 2030.
Q3 fiscal 2026 net sales were $258.7 million, up 10.5% year-over-year, driven by higher volume, pricing, and favorable currency translation.
Orders grew 11% to $247 million, with U.S. orders up 15% and EMEA orders up 3%, the latter largely FX-driven.
Backlog increased 15% year-over-year to $342 million, with increases across all platforms in both short-cycle and project businesses.
Adjusted EBITDA was $39.8 million with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 15.4%, and adjusted EPS grew 11% year-over-year to $0.62.

The Kito Crosby acquisition was funded with a $1.65 billion Term Loan B at SOFR plus 350 basis points, $900 million of senior secured notes at 7.125%, $800 million of perpetual convertible preferred stock, and a new $500 million revolving credit facility, with financing rates coming in below the initial estimate of approximately 8%.

The company expects to realize approximately 20% of the $70 million net run rate cost synergies in year 1, 60% in year 2, and the full 100% in year 3, with year 1 savings expected to be back-end loaded.

Kito Crosby's trailing twelve-month results showed sales of $1.140 billion to $1.150 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $273 million to $283 million, up from the approximately $1.1 billion in revenue and $263 million EBITDA projected when the deal was announced a year ago.
The company expects to use approximately $160 million in net divestiture proceeds from its U.S. power chain hoist and chain operations, expected to close by quarter-end, to pay down the Term Loan B.

The company expects to reduce its net leverage ratio to below 4x by the end of fiscal year 2028 through significant combined free cash flow generation and debt repayment as its primary capital allocation priority.

Adjusted gross margin contracted 170 basis points year-over-year due to unfavorable product mix and tariff impacts, though the company expects to achieve tariff cost neutrality by fiscal year-end and margin neutrality in fiscal 2027.
Operating earnings per diluted share were $1.29, up 16% year-over-year.
The company delivered record total new annualized premiums of $125 million, up 26% year-over-year.
CNO returned $76 million to shareholders in the quarter and $310 million year-to-date.
The company is recording an impairment of $96.7 million in nonoperating income on goodwill and intangibles associated with the Web Benefits Design and DirectPath acquisitions.
CNO is exiting the Worksite fee services business, which contributed a pretax annual loss of approximately $20 million and represented less than 1% of total revenue.
The second Bermuda reinsurance treaty ceded approximately $1.8 billion of Supplemental Health U.S. statutory reserves effective October 1.
The company raised its operating return on equity improvement target for 2027 to 200 basis points, up from the prior target of 150 basis points versus a run rate of approximately 10% in 2024.
Guidance for excess cash flow to the holding company was raised to a range of $365 million to $385 million, up from $200 million to $250 million.
The annual actuarial review resulted in a $41.3 million favorable impact to operating income.
New money investment rates have exceeded 6% for 11 consecutive quarters, with new investments in the quarter comprising approximately $812 million of assets with an average rating of single A.
CVB Financial reported Q3 2025 net earnings of $52.6 million, or $0.38 per share, marking the company's 194th consecutive quarter of profitability spanning more than 48 years.
Return on average tangible common equity was 14.11% and return on average assets was 1.35% for Q3 2025.
Net interest margin increased to 3.33% in Q3 2025, up 28 basis points from 3.05% in Q3 2024.
Noninterest-bearing deposits averaged 59.8% of total deposits in Q3 2025, up from 59.1% in Q3 2024.
Total loans increased by $112 million, or 5% annualized, to $8.47 billion at September 30, 2025.
Loan originations in Q3 2025 were approximately 55% higher than Q3 2024, while year-to-date originations were 57% higher than the same period in 2024.
A $20 million nonperforming loan was paid off in full subsequent to quarter close, with approximately $3 million of interest to be recorded in Q4 2025.
The company sold $65 million of securities yielding 1.3% and reinvested in $214 million of securities yielding approximately 5%, realizing an $8.2 million loss.
Year-to-date, the company repurchased 2.4 million shares at an average price of $18.43.
The company's tangible common equity ratio was 10.1%, common equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 16.3%, and total risk-based capital ratio was 17.1% at September 30, 2025.
Owens Corning generated Q3 2025 revenue of $2.7 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $638 million, delivering a 24% adjusted EBITDA margin.
The company recorded a $780 million noncash goodwill impairment charge in its Doors business due to near-term market weakness affecting accounting valuation assumptions.
Free cash flow for Q3 was $752 million compared to $558 million in the same period last year, benefiting from disciplined working capital management and lower cash taxes.
Through the first three quarters of 2025, the company returned over $700 million to shareholders of the $2 billion committed to returning over 2025 and 2026.

Q4 Roofing revenue is anticipated to decline mid-20% versus prior year, with ARMA market shipments expected to decline high 20% due to lower storm activity and year-end inventory reductions.
For the first time in a decade, no named storms in the Atlantic made landfall in the U.S. during Q3, significantly impacting roofing demand.

The company has identified an additional $75 million of structural cost savings in Doors through operational improvements and plant consolidations, beyond the $125 million in enterprise synergies already on track.

In Q3 2025, 204 new patients started IBTROZI, representing over 15 new patient starts per week, which is 5x greater than the next most recent therapeutic benchmark (Augtyro) in ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
Q3 2025 total revenue was $13.1 million, including $7.7 million in net product revenue from IBTROZI in the company's first full quarter as a commercial stage company.

The median duration of response for TKI-naive patients treated with IBTROZI increased to 50 months from 44 months based on an August 2025 data cutoff, with a supplemental NDA planned to be submitted by the end of the week.
Payer coverage for IBTROZI reached more than 80% of covered lives by end of Q3, up from 58% just two months prior.
The company ended Q3 with $549 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, with an additional $50 million available under a term loan agreement until June 30, 2026.
Nuvation Bio expects a $25 million milestone payment from Nippon Kayaku in Q4 2025 following IBTROZI's approval for reimbursement in Japan.
The company stated that current annualized net revenue based on Q3 new patient starts would be more than $55 million if those patients remain on IBTROZI for 12 months.
R&D expenses for Q3 were $28.8 million and SG&A expenses were $37.4 million, with the commercial field team rightsized at 47 oncology account managers with no expected increases.

The company decided not to pursue a head-to-head study of safusidenib against vorasidenib in low-grade glioma due to costs exceeding $100 million, instead focusing on a registration-enabling Phase III study in high-grade IDH1-mutant glioma with approximately 300 patients expected to complete in 2029.

Management stated they are comfortable with 2026 consensus estimates of approximately $115 million in revenue and are in advanced discussions with potential IBTROZI commercialization partners in Europe expected to conclude in Q4.

Q1 2026 total revenue was $239.2 million, declining sequentially by $1.3 million (0.6%), with EBITDA as adjusted decreasing sequentially by $6.6 million to $70.2 million (29.3% margin), though margin expanded 150 basis points year-over-year.

Cogent entered a non-binding LOI to sell 10 of 24 former Sprint data centers with expected closing in early summer 2026, with aggregate proceeds substantially more than $144 million, and committed the vast majority of proceeds to debt buyback at Cogent Communications Group.

On-net revenue (including wavelengths) grew 9.1% year-over-year to $149.2 million and now represents 62% of total revenue (up from 47% at Sprint closing), while less profitable off-net revenue declined 17% year-over-year to $89 million.

Management expects to exceed its multi-year guidance of 200 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion in 2026 but will not repeat 2025's ~800 bps improvement, with ~$45 million in annualized cost savings (remaining synergies plus integration costs of <$3 million/month) expected to disappear by 2027.

IPv4 leasing revenue grew 25% year-over-year to $18 million at a stable $0.40 per address ARPU, with 15 million of 37.8 million owned addresses leased; on-net monthly churn was stable at 1.2% and off-net churn improved to 1.7% from 1.9%.
Net sales for Q2 fiscal 2026 increased 6.4% to $221.5 million from $208.2 million in the prior year.
Gross profit for Q2 fiscal 2026 increased 3.5% to a second quarter record of $42.7 million.
Net bank debt decreased by $24.6 million during the fiscal 2026 six-month period to $56.7 million from $81.4 million.
The company generated $31.9 million in operating cash flow for the fiscal 2026 six-month period compared with $2 million for the prior year six-month period.
The company repurchased 287,910 shares for $3.4 million at an average share price of $11.65 during the first half of fiscal 2026.
Operating income for Q2 fiscal 2026 increased 30.8% to $16.4 million from $12.5 million in the prior year.
EBITDA before noncash and onetime cash expenses was $95.5 million for the 12 months ended September 30, 2025.
Total liquidity remains strong with cash and availability of approximately $161 million.
Interest expense for Q2 decreased by $1.5 million to $12.7 million from $14.2 million a year ago due to lower outstanding balances and lower interest rates.
One of the company's largest customers delayed purchases by approximately $14.8 million, which management expects will result in increased orders during the second half of the fiscal year.

Avanos delivered full year 2025 net sales of $701 million, exceeding the revised guidance range, and generated $0.94 of adjusted diluted earnings per share at the high end of the revised earnings guidance.
The Specialty Nutrition Systems segment grew over 8% organically in 2025, with short-term enteral feeding posting double-digit growth globally and long-term feeding growing high single digits.

The Pain Management and Recovery segment's operating profit improved 270 basis points year-over-year to 4%, while normalized organic sales grew 2.3% excluding FX and exited low-growth product lines.
The radiofrequency ablation (RFA) business posted full year double-digit organic growth compared to 2024, with particular strength in ESENTEC and TRIDENT product lines.
Avanos ended 2025 with $90 million of cash on hand and $100 million of debt outstanding, with leverage meaningfully below 1 turn for several quarters.
Full year 2025 free cash flow was $43 million, higher than anticipated, and 2026 capital expenditures are expected to be approximately $25 million, about $7 million lower than 2025.
The Nexus Medical acquisition contributed approximately $5 million in revenue in 2025 and is expected to deliver double-digit organic growth in 2026 and beyond.
Consolidated organic sales growth for strategic segments is expected to be approximately 5% in 2026, with SNS growing mid- to high single digits and PM&R growing low to mid-single digits organically.

Management expects 2026 revenue of approximately $12.6 billion, representing continued strong growth from the $11.65 billion expected for 2025.
Silvus revenue expectations for 2025 were raised from $475 million to $500 million, with 20% growth expected in 2026 and EPS contribution of $0.30-$0.40 (up from prior $0.20 guidance).

Tariff headwinds of $70-$80 million impacted the second half of 2025, with additional headwinds expected in Q1 and Q2 of 2026 before lapping.
APX NEXT connected devices are now expected to reach 300,000 by end of 2026, up from the prior expectation of 200,000 by end of 2025.

The company secured three large D-Series infrastructure upgrade orders totaling $276 million from Colorado ($110 million), Tennessee ($84 million), and another U.S. state/local customer ($82 million).
Command center revenue grew 16% in Q3, and the company expects full-year Software and Services growth of low double digits, up from earlier guidance of 10%.
The Andersons reported Q4 2025 adjusted net income of $70 million or $2.04 per diluted share, compared to $47 million or $1.36 per diluted share in Q4 2024, representing a record fourth quarter EPS.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $337 million compared to $363 million in 2024, while Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $137 million compared to $117 million in Q4 2024.

The Renewables segment generated Q4 2025 pretax income attributable to the company of $54 million, a significant increase from $17 million in Q4 2024, driven by full ownership of 4 ethanol plants and record production.

The Skyland Grain acquisition contributed just shy of $20 million in EBITDA for 2025, with management expecting $25 million to $35 million in EBITDA from Skyland in 2026.
Ethanol board crush margins were up $0.15 per gallon year-over-year in Q4 2025, though partially offset by higher natural gas costs and firmer Eastern Corn basis.

Only about 10% of patients diagnosed with geographic atrophy are currently treated with complement inhibitors, leaving substantial room for market growth.

Quarterly shipments increased 9.8% year-over-year, driven by contributions from recent acquisitions and stronger demand across nonresidential construction markets.
